CHIEF COMPLAINT
Follow-up regarding recent hospitalization for infection, spasms, lightheadedness, and constipation.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient is a 39-year-old female with history of quadriplegia due to prior spinal cord injury. She was admitted to District Regional Hospital on 06/29/2021 and discharged on 07/02/2021. During that admission, she presented with increasing concerns for spasms, lightheadedness, significant constipation, and diaphoresis. She was febrile in the emergency department with elevated white blood cell count of 23,000. She had concerns for urinary tract infection and was treated with IV antibiotic therapy. She experienced labile blood pressure, headache, and vomiting. She has a suprapubic catheter. Cultures were obtained. She slowly improved and was discharged after clinical improvement of symptoms. Patient believes the hospitalization was more likely due to dysreflexia from her quadriplegia rather than a true urinary tract infection, noting that constipation was the primary issue. She reports that after discharge, when she had a bowel movement at home, she felt much better. She went to the hospital because her blood pressure was out of control, which was giving her a headache and making her vomit. She states she is now back to her normal self. She denies pain or discomfort.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Patient denies current pain or discomfort. No acute symptoms reported at this time.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Quadriplegia due to prior spinal cord injury
Chronic constipation
History of dysreflexia

MEDICATIONS
Miralax daily
Lactulose for severe constipation
Vitamin C
Multivitamins

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient tends to stay indoors more during hot weather. She acknowledges staying mostly inside during the hot period prior to hospitalization.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Lungs: Clear to auscultation bilaterally. Patient taken through several deep breaths with normal breathing. No abnormal findings noted.
General: Patient denies pain or discomfort anywhere.

RESULTS
Recent hospitalization labs showed white blood cell count of 23,000. Urine cultures were obtained and reviewed but were not impressive. Patient's white count has been normal in prior years. X-rays were performed during hospitalization but no CT scan was done.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Acute to chronic constipation: Patient has good bowel regimen with miralax as primary treatment and lactulose for severe constipation. Patient feels hospitalization was related to constipation and dysreflexia rather than true urinary tract infection. Doctor discussed that dehydration during hot weather can worsen constipation. Plan to repeat fasting labs including complete blood count and full cholesterol panel in 2-3 weeks to ensure white blood cells trend downward and to check cholesterol since it has been a while. If white count remains elevated, may indicate something else going on with bowels.

Quadriplegia: Continue current management.

COVID vaccine status: Patient is currently unvaccinated. Discussed concerns about unknown side effects and reports of "vaccine injury." Patient believes she is young and healthy enough to beat COVID despite limited respiratory function and notes she takes vitamin C and multivitamins and is closely monitored. Patient does not receive flu shot. Doctor recommended vaccination, noting patient is high risk given quadriplegia status. Doctor emphasized vaccine is safe, discussed rare side effects such as Guillain-Barré, and noted that 50% of the country has been vaccinated. Doctor expressed concern about patient's risk if she contracts COVID, citing deaths in practice from COVID. Patient agreed to think about it and acknowledged this discussion is helpful. Doctor recommended vaccination as the only true preventative mechanism for COVID and does not believe supplements will help stave off infection.
